definitions.explanation: A small pocket of fluid that forms under the skin, typically caused by burns, friction, or sunburn. A very common everyday health term in Japanese.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}に{水|みず}ぶくれができた。
examples.english: I got a blister on my foot.

examples.japanese: やけどで{水|みず}ぶくれが{出来|でき}てしまった。
examples.english: I ended up getting a blister from a burn.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}ぶくれを{潰|つぶ}すと{感染|かんせん}する{恐|おそ}れがあるので、{自分|じぶん}で{触|さわ}らないほうがいい。
examples.english: Popping a blister can lead to infection, so it's better not to touch it yourself.

notes:
A compound of {水|みず} (water) and ぶくれ (swelling, from {膨|ふく}れる). Refers to a fluid-filled blister on the skin caused by burns, friction, or skin conditions. Very common in everyday health vocabulary.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水|みず}ぶくれができる: to get a blister
- {水|みず}ぶくれを{潰|つぶ}す: to pop a blister
- {水|みず}ぶくれが{破|やぶ}れる: a blister bursts

CAUSES:
- やけど (burn)
- {靴|くつ}ずれ (shoe friction)
- {日焼|ひや}け (sunburn)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マメ — callus or blister (from friction, often on hands)
- {火|ひ}ぶくれ — burn blister (specifically from heat)
- {腫|は}れ — swelling (more general)
